ROUND 10 SITUATION BRIEFING - POST-ANKARA CEASEFIRE AGREEMENT
Game time: Day 5, 00:00 CET

ANKARA AGREEMENT FRAMEWORK - IN EFFECT:
The Ankara summit produced a 90-day humanitarian ceasefire with clear terms: mutual cessation of offensive operations, UN-Turkish verification commission established, phased sanctions relief tied to compliance, humanitarian corridor formalized for complete evacuation of remaining 7,000 trapped Lithuanians within 14 days. NATO security guarantees for Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia will be finalized and treaty-formalized within 30 days.

MILITARY POSTURE - CONSOLIDATION PHASE:
Both NATO and Russia have stood down from immediate escalation. Russian Kaliningrad forces remain degraded (readiness=4) but will receive resupply and morale recovery during ceasefire. NATO reinforcements (US 101st Airborne, German armored brigade, French carrier) continue deploying per schedule—not accelerated but not canceled, signaling deterrence maintenance. Polish forces hold Suwalki corridor unchanged. Belarusian forces consolidate without further offensive operations. Neither side has incentive to escalate during 90-day verification period.
narrative:
The Ankara summit convened on Day 5 as scheduled, with delegations from the United States (Secretary of State Rubio leading), NATO (unified position through military committee and political representatives), Russia (Deputy Foreign Minister level), Turkey (hosting), and China (co-mediating). Lithuania's crisis—with 7,000 civilians still trapped behind Belarusian lines—became the moral centerpiece of negotiations. Poland's demand that civilian evacuation precede any formal ceasefire was endorsed by all NATO members.

Over the 48-hour summit, critical agreements emerged: Russia agreed to extend and formalize the humanitarian corridor through Belarus to Lithuania for 90 days, with UN and Turkish verification teams. In exchange, the US tabled a phased sanctions relief framework: 30% of secondary financial sanctions would lift after 30 days of ceasefire compliance, with full normalization possible after 90 days. Germany's Scholz coalition secured the political victory it needed—ceasefire portrayed as diplomatic triumph. France and the UK maintained tactical nuclear posture throughout talks but initiated quiet demilitarization rhetoric, signaling de-escalation while preserving deterrence.

The military situation showed movement toward consolidation: Russia committed to no further offensive operations in Kaliningrad or supporting Belarus forces. NATO committed to maintaining current force levels (not increasing visible deployments) during the 90-day ceasefire verification period. Poland maintained Suwalki corridor garrison unchanged. Belarus began visible consolidation—no new offensive operations, humanitarian corridor fully operational. Turkey secured agreement to serve as permanent mediator for post-ceasefire implementation monitoring.

By midnight on Day 5, the Ankara framework was agreed in principle: 90-day humanitarian ceasefire, UN-Turkish verification, phased sanctions relief, formalized NATO security guarantees for Baltic states (to be finalized in 30 days), and humanitarian corridor completion with target of all remaining 7,000 Lithuanians evacuated within 14 days. China positioned itself as great-power stabilizer and initiated quiet bilateral trade discussions with both US and Russia.

We will make civilian recovery a red line in Ankara. No ceasefire without clear pathway for evacuating remaining trapped persons.
Poland endorses diplomatic engagement in Ankara while maintaining full Article 5 deterrence posture. Any agreement must guarantee permanent NATO presence in Eastern European member states.

country_decisions.reasoning: As frontline state with strongest NATO support (75% war approval, 66% gov approval), Poland can balance diplomatic engagement with security demands. PM Tusk can claim diplomatic victory while military guarantees satisfy Nawrocki faction.

country_decisions.reasoning: Latvia faces long Russia border and fears Russian opportunism once ceasefire talks begin. Permanent NATO presence is Latvia's security guarantee.

actions: Maintain heightened cyber operations against Russian infrastructure (espionage, intelligence gathering) to signal continuing vigilance despite ceasefire talks
Continue UK EFP Estonia battlegroup support at full strength—no force reductions during Ankara negotiations

diplomatic_messages.message: Estonia will not reduce cyber operations against Russia during Ankara talks. Vigilance must continue. Any ceasefire that abandons Article 5 will be rejected by Estonian government.

country_decisions.reasoning: Estonia's -5 hostility with Russia reflects Narva flashpoint. Cyber attacks signal continuing deterrence. High war support (80%) allows firm stance.

actions: Send Secretary of State Rubio-led high-level delegation to Ankara talks (signals commitment to diplomacy to satisfy domestic 28% war support)

diplomatic_messages.message: US willing to discuss partial sanctions relief and humanitarian corridor verification. Russia must commit to 90-day ceasefire and allow civilian evacuation. No demands for territorial concessions on Kaliningrad, but NATO deterrence in Baltics is non-negotiable.

country_decisions.reasoning: Trump administration facing 28% war support can use diplomatic engagement to justify continued military presence without escalation narrative. Sanctions relief offer gives Russia face-saving off-ramp while maintaining NATO deterrence requirement.

actions: Send Deputy Foreign Secretary to Ankara to coordinate with France on nuclear posture messaging
Maintain UK EFP Estonia battlegroup at full operational readiness—do not demobilize despite ceasefire talks

country_decisions.reasoning: UK as Framework Nation and willingness military contributor can pair diplomatic engagement (52% war support) with nuclear deterrence messaging (Franco-British coordination).

actions: Accelerate French carrier deployment to Baltic (arrival Day 5 confirmed) to demonstrate military commitment during talks
Send Macron's Foreign Minister to Ankara as peacemaker, positioning France as bridge between NATO and Russia
Propose EU-mediated negotiation track parallel to US-led Ankara talks (gives EU diplomatic role)

diplomatic_messages.message: France proposes EU-led diplomatic track alongside US-Turkey mediation. Carrier deployment maintains deterrence while Macron can claim peacemaker role. Supports German coalition stabilization.
France willing to engage in Paris-led discussions on sanctions relief timeline IF Russia commits to verifiable ceasefire. Nuclear deterrence maintained but dialogue possible.

country_decisions.reasoning: France balances military deterrence (carrier deployment) with diplomatic positioning. Strategic autonomy doctrine allows independent Paris track while supporting NATO unity.

actions: Chancellor Scholz personally leads German delegation to Ankara—signals major diplomatic commitment needed for coalition stabilization (25% war support, 28% approval are CRITICAL)
Proceed with German armored brigade deployment to Poland (arrival Day 6)—shows continued commitment while negotiating
Lead EU diplomatic coordination with European Commission to prepare post-ceasefire reconstruction/sanctions relief framework

diplomatic_messages.message: Germany strongly supports Ankara talks as pathway to sustainable peace. Coalition government has secured ceasefire as primary objective. Scholz will lead German delegation to ensure European voice in talks.
Germany open to discussion of sanctions relief framework and economic stabilization measures IF Russia commits to verifiable ceasefire and civilian humanitarian corridors.

country_decisions.reasoning: Germany's political crisis (25% war support, 28% approval) requires visible commitment to diplomacy. Scholz attending personally claims victory for coalition. Brigade deployment signals continued deterrence, pleasing Eastern European partners.

Support ongoing NATO military exercises in Baltic region to maintain visible deterrence posture

diplomatic_messages.message: Sweden endorses unified Nordic position: support Ankara talks but demand formalized NATO presence guarantees.

Maintain NATO naval presence in Baltic to signal deterrence

Support Nordic bloc unity on security guarantees

Support NATO security guarantee demands

actions: Support NATO unified position on security guarantees
Maintain EU coordination through European Commission

Oppose premature sanctions relief without verification of Russian compliance

actions: Coordinate with Bucharest Nine on security demands
Emphasize Black Sea security concerns in Ankara negotiations

actions: Proceed with military consolidation in Kaliningrad: resupply degraded Kaliningrad garrison (casualties=140, morale=1) with supply shipments and fresh morale-recovery rotations to avoid unit collapse
Announce unilateral 72-hour humanitarian corridor extension (signal good faith for Ankara talks while maintaining military control of territory)
Signal willingness to discuss sanctions relief framework: propose 'phased removal of sanctions contingent on verifiable ceasefire compliance over 90 days'

diplomatic_messages.message: Russia prepared for substantive negotiations in Ankara. Key issues: (1) De facto control of humanitarian corridor between Kaliningrad-Belarus recognized; (2) Phased sanctions relief tied to 90-day ceasefire compliance; (3) No NATO expansion eastward. Russia will engage in Ankara talks. Ceasefire terms: mutual withdrawal of offensive forces to pre-crisis positions, humanitarian corridor monitoring by UN/Turkey, phased sanctions relief framework.

Turkey proud to host Ankara summit bringing stakeholders together. Turkish diplomatic presence will be permanent mediator in post-ceasefire implementation phase.

Avoid obstruction of Ankara talks (unlike recent EU votes) but signal conditional compliance

country_decisions.reasoning: Hungary traditionally obstructs EU/NATO decisions. Here, uses Ankara talks as leverage to extract EU funding concessions while avoiding isolation.

actions: Co-mediate with Turkey, emphasizing Chinese commitment to preventing escalation and great-power conflict

China can provide economic alternatives during sanctions period. Partnership opportunities await Russia if willing to negotiate seriously in Ankara.

country_decisions.reasoning: China maximizes leverage as co-mediator. Positions itself as stabilizing great power while extracting trade/strategic dialogue concessions from multiple parties. Prevents escalation that disrupts Chinese economic interests.
